scenario: logical/LDET.8.3 with the justifiers in the other order (LDET.8.3.1: the same fact set whichever justifier activated first). TrigB is asserted and pumped, so `from_b` justifies Shared first, then TrigA is asserted and pumped. TrigB, now the first justifier, is retracted and pumped. Shared must still be live on `from_a`'s support: a Probe makes `read_back` log it exactly once. A coalescence that kept only the first justifier's support, or that let the first retraction end the fact, passes neither this nor LDET.8.3, whichever runtime-internal order it favours.
rules_ds:
schema TrigA scope logical:
    v: Int key

schema TrigB scope logical:
    v: Int key

schema Shared scope logical:
    v: Int key

schema Probe scope logical:
    n: Int key

rule from_a:
    TrigA
->
    emit Shared logical v: 1

rule from_b:
    TrigB
->
    emit Shared logical v: 1

rule read_back:
    Probe
    Shared s
->
    log info "shared {s.v}"
